items.originalTitle: Why Charles Leclerc didn’t yield Mexico GP lead after cutting Turn 5
items.summaryEn: Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc has detailed how he snatched and retained the lead from Lewis Hamilton at the Mexico Grand Prix, and the reasoning behind not yielding the position after his illegal overtake at Turn 5.
detailZh: 为什么查尔斯·勒克莱尔在5号弯切弯后没有让出墨西哥大奖赛的领先位置
查尔斯·勒克莱尔详细说明了他和法拉利决定在非法超越队友刘易斯·汉密尔顿后不让出领先位置的理由
查尔斯·勒克莱尔，法拉利，刘易斯·汉密尔顿，法拉利，马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队
法拉利F1车手查尔斯·勒克莱尔深入谈到了他在墨西哥大奖赛上颇具争议的驾驶，更具体地说，是他从刘易斯·汉密尔顿手中抢走并保住领先的方式。
勒克莱尔在起步时向杆位发车的队友发起挑战争夺领先，汉密尔顿在第一组弯道中守住了位置。随后这位摩纳哥车手在4号弯外侧发动攻势，虽然他在弯心处处于领先，但两辆车都冲得太深，最终完全驶离了赛道。
汉密尔顿缓缓驶回赛道，将位置丢给了马克斯·维斯塔潘，而勒克莱尔则切过5号弯并保持在前方。由于超出赛道限制获得了持久优势，他本应让队友重新超过，但那样做也会把位置让给红牛。
最终，勒克莱尔仍保持在对手之前，并因违规被罚时五秒。
“刘易斯和我都尝试了非常晚的刹车，我们都没能过弯，我显然切了赛道，”这位摩纳哥车手回忆道。
“最终在5号弯之后，维斯塔潘夹在中间，这让情况更加混乱。和车队沟通时，我并没有得到明确的反馈，我觉得情况足够混乱，所以保持了位置，我原本预计会有某种处罚。然后我们付出了代价。”
夏尔·勒克莱尔，法拉利；刘易斯·汉密尔顿，法拉利
“我们和车队简短地谈了谈，试图理解[该怎么做]。我问‘我现在该怎么办？’这总是非常棘手——显然在那种情况下你必须做点什么，但那是第二名，还是第三名？最后我继续跑了。显然这肯定会成为下次简报会上的一个话题。”
这一决定激怒了汉密尔顿，他在无线电中反复向比赛工程师卡洛·桑蒂抱怨。“问题是他有干净空气，不必像我们其他人那样管理轮胎。他应该把位置还回来，”他谈到勒克莱尔时说，随后又加倍强调：“干事们基本上是在把这场胜利拱手送给夏尔。”
尽管勒克莱尔有争议地保住了领先位置，但这次队内事件发生在今年法拉利车手之间偶有摩擦的背景下。
因此，当被问及法拉利的交战规则时，这位29岁的车手淡化了这一情况：“我的意思是，我们正在为胜利而战，所以当然，他和我在场上留下的空间会非常小。最终，我们在进入4号弯时都犯了错误，并不是说我们发生了接触之类的。我们都冲出了赛道，这给了马克斯超车的机会。
“我不认为这应该成为那么大的话题。当然，当时很接近，1号弯到3号弯非常接近，但我预料到了，这是在为领先而战。在5号弯我们都犯了错误，我付出了罚时的代价，然后你可以争论这是否足够。而刘易斯随后在5号弯因为马克斯付出了代价。”
当被追问他和汉密尔顿是否需要更多规则时，勒克莱尔思考道：“我们显然会讨论这件事。我不知道他是否对我的所作所为非常不满，因为我觉得他的所作所为也几乎到了极限。我认为他可能对整个情况更生气，对4号弯到5号弯的情况如何处理、罚时等等。所以这肯定是我们会讨论的事情。”
从那时起，勒克莱尔就努力拉开与维斯塔潘的距离，试图减轻处罚带来的影响。他在第24圈结束时将差距扩大到5.243秒，但当他进站时——红牛车手也跟随他进入维修区——荷兰人已经将差距缩小了几十分之一秒。
最终，这对结果没有任何影响。勒克莱尔的进站比维斯塔潘多用了6.3秒，其中1.3秒是处罚造成的，因此这位四届世界冠军轻松取得领先。
在瓦尔特利·博塔斯撞车引发红旗后的第二次起步中，勒克莱尔的比赛每况愈下，一次严重的锁死损坏了SF-26的轮胎——尤其是左前轮。
“我认为我们的速度相当不错，但不幸的是在第二次重新起步后，一切都变得有些困难，”他哀叹道。
“赛道右侧有很多轮胎碎屑，当我踩刹车时，尽管我没有施加很大的刹车压力，还是立刻锁死了，直接冲向了轮胎的帘布层。所以最后一段 stint 非常棘手。”
勒克莱尔最终在方格旗下列第四——仍然连续第六次获得前四名完赛。
detailEn: Why Charles Leclerc didn’t yield Mexico GP lead after cutting Turn 5
Charles Leclerc has detailed the reasoning behind his and Ferrari’s decision not to yield the lead after he illegally overtook team-mate Lewis Hamilton
Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing
Ferrari Formula 1 driver Charles Leclerc has delved into his controversial Mexico Grand Prix drive, more specifically the way he snatched – and retained – the lead from Lewis Hamilton.

Leclerc challenged his polesitting team-mate for the lead at the start, with Hamilton holding him off over the first sequence of corners. The Monegasque then launched an attack around the outside of Turn 4, but while he was ahead at the apex, both cars went deep and ended up fully off the track.

Hamilton trundled back on track, losing a position to Max Verstappen, while Leclerc cut Turn 5 and stayed out in front. Having gained a lasting advantage from exceeding track limits, he was expected to let the sister car back through, but that would have entailed giving up a position to the Red Bull too.
In the end, Leclerc remained ahead of his rivals, copping a five-second penalty for the infringement.
“Lewis and I both tried to brake very late, we both didn't make the corner, I obviously cut the track,” the Monegasque recounted.

“Eventually then after Turn 5 there was Max in between, which made the situation more confusing. And speaking with the team, I didn't really have a clear feedback, and I think it was just confusing enough to keep the position, and I was expecting some kind of penalty. Then we paid the penalty.
Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari

“We spoke briefly with the team to try and understand [what to do]. I asked ‘What should I do now?’ It's always very tricky – obviously in that situation you have to do something, but is it second, is it third? At the end I kept going. Obviously it's going to be a bit of a talking point, for sure, next briefing.”

The decision drew the ire of Hamilton, who repeatedly complained to race engineer Carlo Santi on the radio. “The problem is he's got clean air, and doesn't have to manage like the rest of us. He should just give the place back,” he said of Leclerc, before doubling down: “The stewards are basically handing Charles this win.”
Regardless of Leclerc’s controversial move to retain the lead, the intra-team incident came amid occasional friction between the Ferrari drivers this year.

Consequently asked about the rules of engagement at Ferrari, the 29-year-old played the situation down: “I mean, we are fighting for the win, so of course there's going to be very little margin left from him and from me. [In] the end, we both did a mistake going into Turn 4, it's not like we had contact or whatsoever. We both went straight and that gave the opportunity for Max to overtake.

“I don't think it should be that much of a talking point. Of course it was close, Turn 1 to 3 was very close, but I was expecting it, [in a] fight for the lead. For [Turn] 5 we both made a mistake, I paid with a penalty, then you can argue whether it's enough or not. And Lewis then paid out of [Turn] 5 with Max.”

Pressed on whether he and Hamilton needed more rules going forward, Leclerc pondered: “We will talk about it obviously. I don't know if he was very unhappy with what I did because I felt like it was very much on the limit also what he did. I think he was maybe more angry with the whole situation, how the situation was dealt in [Turns] 4-5 with the penalty, etc. So this is something we'll talk about for sure.”

From then on, Leclerc worked at pulling away from Verstappen in an attempt to mitigate the impact of his penalty. He brought the gap up to 5.243s at the end of lap 24, but by the time he pitted – with the Red Bull following him into the pits – the Dutchman had cut his deficit by a few tenths.

In the end, this made no difference to the outcome. Leclerc’s pitstop was 6.3s longer than Verstappen’s, with 1.3s unaccounted for by the penalty, so the four-time world champion comfortably took the lead.
Leclerc’s race went from bad to worse at the second start, following the red flag for Valtteri Bottas’ crash, with a hefty lock-up that damaged the SF-26’s tyres – especially the front-left.
“I think we had quite a good pace, but unfortunately on the second restart everything went a bit more difficult,” he lamented.

“There was quite a lot of marbles on the right side of the track, and when I went on the brake, even though I didn't put a massive amount of brake pressure, I locked up straight away and I went to the cord of the tyres. So the last stint was very tricky.”
Leclerc consequently ended up fourth under the chequered flag – still scoring a sixth consecutive top-four finish.

items.originalTitle: F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali releases touching statement after Kimi Antonelli's title win
detailZh: F1 CEO安东内利在基米·安东内利夺冠后发表感人声明
Formula 1 CEO安东内利庆祝基米·安东内利在墨西哥大奖赛上取得的具有历史意义的冠军胜利
Stefano Domenicali，Formula One Group的CEO
对于梅赛德斯车迷来说。这里是关于银箭的最新消息，包括来自Brackley和Brixworth的F1新闻、车手更新、赛车发展和比赛分析。
一级方程式CEO斯蒂法诺·多梅尼卡利表示，在基米·安东内利在墨西哥大奖赛成为该系列赛最年轻冠军后，'整个国家都将为之庆祝'。
这位20岁的年轻人也成为73年来首位意大利世界冠军，上一位是1953年的阿尔贝托·阿斯卡里。梅赛德斯车手在阿维莫罗·赫尔曼诺斯·罗德里格斯赛道上获得第三名，在获胜者马克斯·维斯塔潘和法拉利的刘易斯·汉密尔顿之后，获得了足够的积分来赢得冠军。
多梅尼卡利在一份声明中表示，'今天，基米·安东内利创造了历史。成为最年轻的一级方程式世界冠军是一项非凡的成就，这是通过非凡的才能、勇气和决心获得的。'
'看到基米成为自1953年阿尔贝托·阿斯卡里以来首位意大利一级方程式世界冠军，我感到无比自豪。73年来，我们的国家一直在等待这一刻，今天整个国家都将庆祝自己的同胞达到我们这项运动的顶峰。
“伟大不仅仅由记录衡量，还在于它激励的世代。基米吸引了全世界数百万粉丝的想象力，并向全世界年轻人证明，通过奉献、信念和努力工作，没有什么是不可能的。今天全世界观看比赛的男女孩子们将会看到，基米证明了最大的梦想可以成为现实。”
“刘易斯·汉密尔顿、法拉利、马克斯·维斯塔潘、红牛车队、安东内利、梅赛德斯”
“安东内利在本赛季已经赢得了九个大奖赛，这是他加入F1的第二年，包括他在蒙扎的家乡赛事，他在2025年取代了汉密尔顿在梅赛德斯的位置。”
“今天，他的名字加入了我们运动中的传奇人物，”意大利人继续说。“F1历史的一个新篇章已经写下，我坚信这只是一个非凡遗产的开始。”
“恭喜基米、梅赛德斯和他的家人取得这一令人难以置信的成就。整个一级方程式社区都为能与他们一起庆祝这个特殊的时刻而感到自豪。”
detailEn: F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali releases touching statement after Kimi Antonelli's title win
Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali has celebrated Kimi Antonelli's historic championship victory at the Mexican Grand Prix
Stefano Domenicali, CEO of the Formula One Group
For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.
Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali says "an entire nation will celebrate" after Kimi Antonelli became the series' youngest champion at the Mexican Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old also became the first Italian world champion in 73 years, since Alberto Ascari in 1953. The Mercedes driver finished third at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez behind race-winner Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, securing enough points to claim the title.

"Today, Kimi Antonelli has made history. Becoming the youngest Formula 1 world champion is an extraordinary achievement, earned through exceptional talent, courage and determination," Domenicali said in a statement.

"It fills me with immense pride to see Kimi become the first Italian Formula 1 world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953. For 73 years, our country has waited for this moment, and today an entire nation will celebrate one of its own reaching the very pinnacle of our sport.

"Greatness is measured not only by records, but by the generations it inspires. Kimi has captured the imagination of millions of fans around the world and shown young people everywhere that there are no limits to what can be achieved through dedication, belief and hard work. Across the world, young boys and girls watching today will see in Kimi someone who proves that the biggest dreams can become reality."
Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes
Antonelli has won nine grands prix so far this season in only his second year in F1, including his home race at Monza, having replaced Hamilton at Mercedes in 2025.

"Today, his name joins the legends of our sport," the Italian continued. "A new chapter in Formula 1 history has been written, and I firmly believe this is only the beginning of an extraordinary legacy.
"Congratulations to Kimi, Mercedes and his family on this incredible achievement. The entire Formula 1 community is proud to celebrate this special moment with them."

items.titleZh: 汉密尔顿要求法拉利内部严肃沟通
items.summaryZh: 墨西哥大奖赛后，汉密尔顿认为首圈与勒克莱尔的碰撞让法拉利错失胜利，要求车队在内部进行严肃沟通。
items.originalTitle: Hamilton demands 'serious talks' after latest Leclerc incident
items.summaryEn: After the Mexican Grand Prix, Lewis Hamilton said Ferrari needed serious talks behind the scenes, believing the opening-lap incident with Charles Leclerc cost the team a win.
detailZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿表示，在与夏尔·勒克莱尔发生首圈事故后，法拉利F1车队需要在幕后进行一些“严肃的沟通”，他认为这起事故让车队错失了墨西哥大奖赛的胜利。
从杆位起步的汉密尔顿在起步后的最初几个弯道保持领先，尽管他的队友一度升至第二并向他发起挑战。然而，他在通往4号弯的路段再次遭到进攻。
当勒克莱尔试图从外线超车时，两人都刹车过晚。
勒克莱尔最终切过草地，在5号弯后重返赛道，并已取得领先；而汉密尔顿在4号弯出口跑宽，失去速度，让身后的马克斯·维斯塔潘在不久后完成超越。
那次事故被证明是决定性的，因为勒克莱尔因此受到的5秒罚时，让他在首次进站后落到了维斯塔潘身后。
在比赛的剩余时间里，包括一次红旗和安全车重启，汉密尔顿始终无法找到超越维斯塔潘的办法，最终以第二名完赛，而他认为法拉利本有速度做得更好。
汉密尔顿在整场比赛中反复表达不满，认为勒克莱尔的行为只被罚5秒太轻了。
在以第二名输给维斯塔潘后，他觉得这一系列事件让法拉利付出的代价，是需要在内部讨论的事情。
“艰难，真是艰难的一天，”他说。“我认为我们今天有足够的速度赢下比赛，但事与愿违。你知道，我们会回去复盘，弄清楚在幕后还能做些什么。”
汉密尔顿表示，车手简报会上达成的共识是，如果车手在第一或第二组弯道切过草地，就应该让出位置——他也在赛后质疑为何勒克莱尔的处罚如此宽松。
“显然，去年我因为他的那个同样动作被罚了10秒，”汉密尔顿说。
“但最终，正是那件事让我们今天丢掉了胜利，我认为我们肯定需要在幕后进行一些严肃的讨论。”
勒克莱尔：汉密尔顿的驾驶也“非常接近极限”
勒克莱尔不同意汉密尔顿关于此事特别严重的评估，因为双方没有接触，而且在一场争夺胜利的战斗中两人都犯了错误。
“我们显然会谈谈这件事，”他说。“我不知道他是否对我的所作所为非常不满，因为我觉得他的所作所为也非常接近极限。
“我认为他可能更多是对整个情况感到愤怒，即第4-5弯的情况处理方式、罚时等等。这肯定是我们会讨论的事情。”
勒克莱尔认为两人在争夺中的方式并无异常，因为并没有车队指令阻止他们缠斗。
“我的意思是，我们正在为胜利而战，所以当然，他和我的余量都会非常小，”他说。
“最后我们俩在进入4号弯时都犯了错误，我们并没有任何接触。我们都直行了，这给了马克斯超车的机会。
“所以我认为这不应该成为那么大的话题。当然，很接近，1号、2号、3号弯都非常接近，但我本来就预料到这会是一场领先位置的争夺。”
“在5号弯我们俩都犯了错。我付出了罚时的代价，然后你可以争论这够不够，而刘易斯随后在5号弯和马克斯之间也付出了代价。”
勒克莱尔还解释说，事故发生后他曾与车队讨论是否要交还位置，但情况很复杂，因为维斯塔潘插到了他和汉密尔顿之间。
“我们和车队简短地谈了谈，试图理解情况，”他说。“我问‘我现在该怎么办？’这总是非常棘手。
“显然在那种情况下，你多少会预期自己必须做点什么，但那是第二名，还是第三名……最后我继续跑了。
“显然，在下次简报会上，这肯定会成为一点讨论话题。”
detailEn: Lewis Hamilton says the Ferrari Formula 1 team needs some "serious talks" behind the scenes after the opening lap incident with Charles Leclerc that he thinks cost his team a Mexican Grand Prix win.

Having started from pole position, Hamilton had kept his lead at the start through the opening sequence of corners, despite an initial challenge from his team-mate who had got up to second. However, he came under a fresh attack on the run to Turn 4.
As Leclerc attempted to go around the outside, the pair managed to outbrake themselves.

Leclerc ended up cutting across the grass and rejoining after Turn 5, having moved into the lead, while Hamilton ran wide at the Turn 4 exit and lost momentum – allowing Max Verstappen behind him to get past shortly afterwards.
That incident proved decisive as the five-second penalty that Leclerc picked up dropped him behind Verstappen at their first pitstops.

For the remainder of the race, which included a red flag and safety car restart, Hamilton was unable to find a way past Verstappen as he came home second on a day he felt Ferrari had the pace to do better.
Hamilton repeatedly throughout the race expressed his annoyance about Leclerc only picking up a five-second penalty for what he did.
And after finishing second to Verstappen, he felt the way that the events had cost Ferrari was something that needed to be discussed internally.
"A tough, tough day," he said. "I think we had the pace to win today, but it wasn't meant to be. And you know, we'll take it offline and figure out what we can do in the background."

Hamilton said that agreement in the drivers' briefing had been that if drivers cut the grass at the first or second complex of corners then they should give positions – as he also questioned post-race why Leclerc's penalty was so lenient.
"Obviously, last year I got a 10-second penalty for that same move that he did," said Hamilton.
"But ultimately, it was that that lost us the win today, and I think we have to have some serious talks behind the scenes for sure."
Leclerc: Hamilton's driving 'very much on the limit' too
Leclerc did not agree with Hamilton's assessment that the matter was particularly serious, as there had been no contact and both made a mistake in what was a fight for the win.
"We will talk about it, obviously," he said. "I don't know if he was very unhappy with what I did, because I felt like it was very much on the limit, also, what he did.
"I think he was maybe more angry with the whole situation, how the situation was dealt in [Turns] 4-5, with the penalty, etc. This is something we'll talk about for sure."
Leclerc did not see anything out of the ordinary in how the pair had approached their fight though, as there were no team orders preventing them battling.
"I mean we are fighting for the win and so of course there's going to be very little margin left from him and from me," he said.
"At the end we both did a mistake going into Turn 4, it's not like we had contact whatsoever. We both went straight and that gave the opportunity for Max to overtake.
"So I don't think it should be that much of a talking point. Of course it was close, Turn 1, 2, 3 was very close, but I was expecting it to be [in the] fight for the lead.
"For Turn 5 we both made a mistake. I paid with a penalty, then you can argue whether it's enough or not, and Lewis then paid out of Turn 5 with Max."

Leclerc also explained that he had discussed with his team about whether or not to give the position back after the incident, but the situation was complicated because Verstappen had got between himself and Hamilton.
"We spoke briefly with the team to try and understand," he said. "I asked 'what should I do now?' and it's always very tricky.
"And obviously in that situation you kind of expect you have to do something, but is it second, is it third... At the end I kept going.
"Obviously it's going to be a bit of a talking point for sure at the next briefing."
keyPointsZh: 汉密尔顿从杆位起步，起步阶段守住领先，但在4号弯前再次受到勒克莱尔进攻。
勒克莱尔在4号弯外线尝试超车时两人双双刹车过晚，勒克莱尔切过草地并在5号弯后重返赛道时取得领先。
汉密尔顿在4号弯出口跑宽失去速度，随后被维斯塔潘超越。
keyPointsEn: Hamilton started from pole and kept the lead early despite pressure from his team-mate, but came under fresh attack on the run to Turn 4.
Leclerc tried around the outside, both braked too late, and Leclerc cut across the grass and rejoined after Turn 5 in the lead.
Hamilton ran wide at the Turn 4 exit and lost momentum, allowing Max Verstappen behind him to get past shortly afterwards.
